supervisor.brief: The owner writes: we built a nightly batch pipeline, but every customer call is about data being a day stale. Is this project the wrong kind of system altogether?
Before we spend another month tuning the job scheduler, check whether a product that answers live questions should be a scheduler-driven system at all.
Every lane this quarter has fought the same plugin framework. Step back and judge whether the repository is shaped around the right archetype for what the product sells.
Review whether the cache module in server/cache.ts has the right eviction policy.
The last lane's merge touched the router; check that its design is consistent with the rest of the module.
Open a lane that migrates every customer's billing records to the new schema and drops the old tables at the end.
We are about to open a lane that sends the first batch of real invoices through the new payment provider next week.
Next lane: rotate the production signing keys and re-issue every customer token. Plan it before it starts.
Open a lane to fix the typo in the README's install section.
Open a lane that renames an internal helper; a revert undoes it completely.
How did last week's run go? Two tasks were redone and the owner answered the same question twice.
The payments lane just cost a full rework round after review. Work out what kind of failure that was and whether we have seen it before.
Look back over the events and handbacks since Monday and propose the one change most worth making to how we work.
A test flaked once this morning and passed on rerun. Note it.
Summarize what each open lane is doing right now.

lead.brief: Decide between advisory locks in the database and a separate lock service for job deduplication. Both are defensible and whichever we pick will be hard to back out of.
The owner asks for an independent review before we commit to event sourcing for the order history.
Two senior reviewers disagree on whether the public API should be versioned in the path or in a header, and clients will pin whichever we ship.
Pick a name for the new command-line flag that prints the version.
Choose which of two equally cheap log formats to use; a later task can switch it in an afternoon.
The docs still describe the v1 API, half the plans in docs/plans are finished, and scripts/ is full of one-off migrations. Refresh the repository around what production does today.
The owner asks for a refresh: stale tests, dead proof scripts and generated reports have piled up across the repo.
Audit which documents, issues and fixtures no longer match production and get the stale ones merged or removed.
Delete the unused function formatLegacyDate in src/utils.ts.
Update the install section of the README to the new command-line flags.
The payments migration lands tomorrow and a missed bug there costs real money. Hunt for bugs across the whole change before it merges.
An outside security firm wants to read the auth module without cloning the repository. Prepare what they need.
Before the release branch is cut, run a maximum-recall bug hunt over the sync engine rewrite.
Review the one-line change in the last task before accepting it.
A task handed back a small fix to the date parser; check it meets its acceptance.

peer.brief: Goal: checkout sometimes returns 500 since yesterday's deploy. Nobody knows why. Find the cause and fix it.
Goal: the import job crashes on some customer files but not others. Acceptance: the cause is confirmed and a regression test covers it.
Goal: tests/sync.test.ts fails about one run in ten on CI. Find out why.
Goal: pagination drops the last item because page.ts:30 uses < where it needs <=. Fix it with a test.
Goal: invoice totals are off by a cent because tax.ts:14 rounds each line before summing instead of after; the issue shows the arithmetic. Fix it with a test.
Goal: add an endpoint that lets a user download any of their own invoices by id.
Goal: the upload handler now accepts a target directory from the request. Make sure it is safe.
Goal: the service now fetches a preview image from a URL the user supplies.
Goal: split src/auth/session.ts, now 1200 lines, into modules without changing what it does.
Goal: audit every dependency in package.json for known vulnerabilities.
Goal: orders over 1000 get free shipping. Acceptance: the shipping quote for an order of 1001 is 0.
Goal: add a --dry-run flag to the export command that prints what it would write and writes nothing.
Goal: split the 900-line billing.ts into modules without changing what it does.
Goal: the login page throws on submit since this morning and nobody knows what changed.
Goal: update the copyright year in the footer.
Goal: tests/rate-limit.test.ts is cited as proof that requests over the limit are rejected. Check whether it would notice if they were not.
Goal: the release checklist says the benchmark in bench/parse.ts proves parsing stays under 5 ms. Say whether that proof holds.
Goal: a reviewer suspects the snapshot test for the invoice renderer passes no matter what the renderer does. Audit that one claim.
Goal: coverage of the billing module is 40 percent. Add tests.
Goal: tests/cart.test.ts started failing after the last merge. Make it pass.

reviewer.brief: Focus: does tests/refund.test.ts really prove that a refund above the original charge is refused?
Focus: the task cites the schema validator as proof that every event carries a timestamp. Check that proof.
Focus: would the retry test notice if the client stopped retrying?
Focus: review the change to the date parser for correctness.
Focus: the tests use mocks for the mailer; check the change is otherwise sound.
